text:
Maria: heads-up — after the s3-archiver rollout (canary at 09:05 UTC) telemetry-proxy CPU jumped ~3x. Also seeing p99 for /v1/generate up ~50-80ms. Anyone else seeing this? :eyes:

Aj: saw the alert. graph pls (span ingest rate, cpu, exporter queue).

Maria: uploading quick screenshots but numbers: spans/s from frontend -> 12k -> 35k after retention bump, exporter queue length spiked to ~40k, telemetry-proxy CPU 75% -> 220% (across cores). link: https://img.redwood/snap-telemetry-09-05.png

Kevin: what changed in the canary? only s3-archiver + retention window extended from 7d -> 30d, right?

Maria: yep. config diff is small, added s3 exporter and compression. here's the collector fragment I pushed:```yaml
exporters:
  redwood_s3:
    type: s3
    bucket: telemetry-archival
    compress: gzip
service:
  pipelines:
    traces:
      receivers: [otlp]
      processors: [batch]
      exporters: [redwood_s3, otlp/observability]
processors:
  batch:
    send_batch_size: 1024
    timeout: 5s
```

Log snippet from proxy at spike:```text
2026-03-05T09:06:12Z WARN exporter.redwood_s3.batch_processor flush took=823ms items=1024 err=nil
2026-03-05T09:06:12Z INFO exporter.redwood_s3.compress start=0.9ms finish=820ms bytes_out=1.2MB
2026-03-05T09:06:13Z ERROR exporter.redwood_s3.put error=slow-s3-ack
```

Log looks like compression + S3 latency are blocking worker threads — gzip of many spans is expensive. send_batch_size=1024 seems high for this workload.

Logan: also noticed CPU profile: goroutine contention in zlib compress path and flushing to the exporter. probably compressing large batches on the main worker threads.

Aj: two quick mitigations we can try: 1) disable compress: gzip temporarily, 2) lower batch size to 128 and add exporter worker pool. Which should be faster to roll back?

Kevin: disable compress is easiest and least config. batch size change needs config rollout to all collectors. I'd do (1) now.

Maria: rolling compress -> off on canary now. will monitor.```yaml
exporters:
  redwood_s3:
    compress: false
```

sre-bot: [alert] telemetry-proxy CPU > 200% for 3m (host telemetry-proxy-03). Incident page: https://incidents.redwood/5631

Maria: canary patch applied at 09:12 UTC. re-checking metrics — exporter queue dropping, CPU trending down. p99 back to ~+10ms from baseline (still a bit high).

Devon: nice. do we have span size distribution? big single spans could still be expensive to compress.

Maria: yes, tail shows some payloads ~80-120KB (rare). median ~1.2KB. those big ones coincided with spikes.

Aj: follow-up action items I suggest: 1) revert compress by default and make it opt-in per-source, 2) implement async compression workers (offload zlib), 3) lower batch size to 128-256, 4) add throttling when exporter S3 latency > 500ms to avoid buildup.

Kevin: also add instrumentation: per-exporter worker latency histogram, queue-depth alert rule, and split large-span paths into a separate pipeline (no batching).

Logan: agree. small note — gzip on many small spans is often net-negative CPU wise. it helps storage but costs CPU; need a cost model.

Maria: updated runbook snippet for immediate rollback:```sh
# disable compression on collector config
kubectl -n telemetry set env deploy/collector REDWOOD_S3_COMPRESS=false
# reduce batch size
kubectl -n telemetry set env deploy/collector BATCH_SIZE=256
```

sre-bot: [resolved] telemetry-proxy CPU alert resolved at 09:21 UTC.

Maria: marking this thread as postmortem candidate. short RC: combination of (longer retention -> more archival traffic) + large batch size + gzip turned on -> CPU amplification and exporter head-of-line delays causing p99 regressions.

Devon: can we add a perf test to CI that simulates retention + s3 latency so this doesn't regress silently?

Aj: yes. ticket created: INF-1298 "telemetry: simulate s3 slowness + batch compression perf test". I'll own the test.

Kevin: I'll follow up with collector config defaults PR to set compress: false and tuned batch defaults.

Maria: thanks all. quick wins done, long-term work tracked in INF-1298 + INF-1301. :white_check_mark:
